verdicts.reason: Duplicate of T-08: it is the same split between checks that reject and checks that only record, and it brings no evidence of its own. I confirmed the quote at testing-functions.md:548. The card itself says the reference page defines @@check differently, so the vendor docs disagree on the exact semantics being copied. There is also no brief-test runner for it to live in.
verdicts.what_would_change_verdict: T-08's trial finds real contract violations in accepted outputs, which would make the choice between rejecting and recording a live design decision.

verdicts.reason: I confirmed the quote in the exit-code table of ref/baml-cli/test.md. The rule that zero tests run is never green is already program law: ORCHESTRATION-DESIGN-2026-10.md:216 says 'an absent result is never treated as "nothing found"', and coverage must read 16/16 or carry a written waiver. HARNESS-REVIEW-2026-11-01.md:263 adopted skip-aware gates and dropped --passWithNoTests, and RT-01 covers checks that go green without testing anything. A four-state result only matters once a brief-test runner exists, and nobody has decided to build one.
verdicts.what_would_change_verdict: The owner decides to build a brief-test runner. The existing rule would then carry over to it unchanged.

verdicts.reason: The vendor limitation is real (prompt-optimization.md:368-369, confirmed). The harness already keeps infrastructure outcomes apart from content outcomes. A null is never treated as a result (ORCHESTRATION-DESIGN:216). The §4.3 circuit breaker reads fresh nulls as a suspected session limit. With RESEARCH.tool_status set to web_unavailable, an empty result is valid. A scoring rule only bites inside B-13, which is refuted here.
verdicts.what_would_change_verdict: B-13 or another brief-scoring runner is adopted.

verdicts.reason: The half that transfers (record a failed check rather than reject the object) is T-08. The other half would be harmful here: a BAML @assert inside a container silently removes the element (checks-and-asserts.md:11, confirmed), which is exactly the silent drop R-05 documents. Nobody has verified that the StructuredOutput validator supports cross-field if/then rules.
verdicts.what_would_change_verdict: Two things together: confirmation that the tool-layer validator enforces if/then, and a recorded REFUTED verdict without counter-evidence that got past the Fable gate.

verdicts.reason: Replaying already-accepted payloads through the schema that accepted them finds nothing, by construction. Replaying them through the T-08 checks is just T-08's trial. Catching a regression you injected tests the checker, not the briefs. The fixtures already exist (docs/program/evidence/ with a sha256 manifest). However, validating a schema outside Claude Code needs a JSON Schema validator, which is an npm install the owner has not approved, and nothing on the card is BAML-specific.
verdicts.what_would_change_verdict: A planned §5.2 schema edit that might reject output that was valid before, so a backward-compatibility replay would have a real job.

verdicts.reason: agent() returns the validated object or null, with no attempt count (workflow-authoring reference). Per-agent transcripts (agent-<id>.jsonl) could recover the count afterwards, so the card's 'drop it if not observable' branch is wrong. The real break is the benefit: it assumes schema rejections that the program has never recorded. The harness failures on record are session and usage limits: HANDOFF §5.5 says seven agents died on a session limit, and HARNESS-REVIEW:9 records 7 refuters lost to a usage limit. The 10% threshold is arbitrary. The owner also skipped the clinic harness's measurement pipeline because 'a month of research established no gain' (HARNESS-REVIEW:275).
verdicts.what_would_change_verdict: A lane that returned null or junk which its transcript traces to repeated StructuredOutput rejections.

verdicts.reason: The gap is real: the §5.2 schemas contain no description keyword at all. Limits such as '<= 300 words' or 'required on UNVERIFIABLE' live in JS comments the model never sees, and P0–P3 are defined nowhere in the design doc. There is also a recorded signal the assessment missed: 'Eight of twelve skeptic verdicts lowered a severity' (G2-deep-dive-gate:78). Against it: the BAML rendering evidence does not transfer (JSON Schema description is a standard keyword, not a BAML feature). Nobody has checked that descriptions reach the subagent. The inflated severities may also be the intended bias, since skeptics correct them.
verdicts.what_would_change_verdict: First check that a schema description reaches a subagent. Then add one line of definition per P0–P3 value and compare analyst-vs-skeptic severity agreement in the next run that has skeptics against G2's baseline, where 4 of 12 severities survived the skeptic. Adopt if agreement rises clearly. Drop if descriptions do not reach the model.

verdicts.reason: I confirmed the directive in the version notice at the head of each fetched docs page, including claude-code.md. However, every workflow subagent already runs under a platform rule that tool output is data, never instructions (it is in this agent's own system prompt). The reader handled the notice correctly without any new rule, so the observation shows the existing safeguard working. A field for reporting directive text adds bookkeeping, not protection, and no injection incident is on record.
verdicts.what_would_change_verdict: A recorded case of a harness agent acting on directive text in a fetched page.

verdicts.reason: Issue #4590 is confirmed (open, created 2026-08-25, 6 comments). The proposed rule already exists: ORCHESTRATION-DESIGN:219 says FINDINGS are 'sliced to 12 in the script with the dropped count logged (no silent caps)'. FINDINGS.backlog exists so nothing is silently dropped, the workflow reference has a 'No silent caps' pattern, and this sweep's own merge-log.json records every card the dedup folded away. Our tool layer rejects rather than repairs, so the SAP failure mode does not arise here.
verdicts.what_would_change_verdict: Finding a harness script step that filters, de-duplicates or normalises a returned array without logging what it dropped.

verdicts.reason: Duplicate of T-08, built on the same two v0-legacy pages as D-02 and D-07 and with no evidence of its own. Code-computed checks that travel to the judge are T-08's trial.
verdicts.what_would_change_verdict: Same as T-08.

verdicts.reason: I confirmed the quote (SKILL.md:104 'schema_attempts = 2'). The card is a duplicate of D-11. BAML's visible RunResult has nothing in Workflow to map onto, and the benefit (a schema-retry signal) addresses a failure the program has not recorded.
verdicts.what_would_change_verdict: Same as D-11.

verdicts.reason: Duplicate of D-13. Its own source is marketing ('80% token reduction'), which the card itself calls irrelevant to us, so it adds nothing D-13 lacks.
verdicts.what_would_change_verdict: Same as D-13.

verdicts.reason: Two of the four lint checks are already built in or guaranteed by construction. agent() throws on a non-object root, on required not being a subset of properties, and on an unsatisfiable schema (workflow reference). CONTEXT is prepended by a single concatenation, agent(CONTEXT + t.brief) (ORCHESTRATION-DESIGN §4.3 skeleton). The source is BAML's test practice for its own compiler, not for prompts. No hand-edit regression of a brief and no tier leak has been recorded.
verdicts.what_would_change_verdict: A recorded run where a brief went out without its CONTEXT block or named an agent's tier.

verdicts.reason: The evidence is marketing: a README claim, plus open bug #5322 showing the preview breaking. Every Workflow invocation already saves its script to a file, and brief text is constants plus args, so diffing the script already gives the text diff. Prompts assembled from earlier stages' results cannot be dry-run without stubs, and that is P-10.
verdicts.what_would_change_verdict: Briefs assembled from args so heavily that the script source no longer shows the text actually sent.

verdicts.reason: BAML compiles its skills into the binary so the guidance stays matched to the toolchain version across many user projects. tools/ks and its SKILL.md live in the same repository and the same commit (KNOWLEDGE-STORE-DESIGN §7.1, KS-4), so that version skew cannot arise. The store is unbuilt and KS-5 is its stop point, so drift is speculative. A new verb would also grow the 'five verbs to know' surface. The evidence is quality 1.
verdicts.what_would_change_verdict: A KS pull request where SKILL.md named a verb or flag the CLI rejected.

verdicts.reason: Same change as I-01, backed only by Hacker News anecdotes. The harness already has the two-step shape: agents research and think through a full tool loop and in thinking blocks, then format in one final StructuredOutput call. The thread's own point, that hidden-thinking models avoid the trade-off, applies to current Opus and Sonnet subagents.
verdicts.what_would_change_verdict: Same as I-01.

verdicts.reason: I confirmed the quote. The harness already computes counts in code: coverage comes from Object.keys(out).length, and the FINDINGS slice logs its dropped count (ORCHESTRATION-DESIGN §4.3). No §5.2 schema asks a model for a count. The confidence half of the card is T-01.

The harness already uses short stable labels (H-01, S-07b; §4.3) and short card ids. The only long-hash path is `ks capture --fix <40-hex sha>`, which git checks in code, so a mis-echoed hash fails loudly instead of mis-aggregating silently.

verdicts.reason: It is a single post-mortem of BAML's own release process and sits outside the five landing areas. KS-4 also plans the seven HANDOFF §6 shapes as a reviewer checklist, including 'the default path in a fixture became the untested path'. The trial has no control, so a confirmed defect cannot be credited to the added line.

verdicts.reason: Duplicate of T-08, built on a stale 2024 announcement whose test-block syntax the card itself says was later removed.
verdicts.what_would_change_verdict: Same as T-08.

verdicts.reason: Each brief's version can already be recovered: every Workflow run saves its script and has a run id, and the journal records every agent's return value (the evidence README ties outputs to their workflow ids). A brief_sha field only pays inside B-13, which is refuted here.
verdicts.what_would_change_verdict: A brief comparison that actually needed hand-matching of journal entries to brief versions.

verdicts.reason: Three breaks. (1) Inputs are the live repo and the web, not fixed cases. Past W1/W2 runs were at a31924a, so a diff mixes code change with brief change, and open-ended cards disagree almost everywhere, so 'review only disagreements' collapses into reviewing everything. (2) Cost: 10–30 inputs × 2 briefs × 3 repeats is 60–180 agent runs per brief edit, and Opus quota is the program's most often recorded failure (HANDOFF §5.5; HARNESS-REVIEW:9; KS rule K8). (3) Owner precedent: the clinic harness's measurement pipeline was skipped because 'a month of research established no gain' (HARNESS-REVIEW:275), and its WF-02 baseline-vs-treatment trial produced identical acceptance and null token figures (KS design:189). No brief-edit regression has been recorded.
verdicts.what_would_change_verdict: A recorded brief edit that flipped verdicts. If that happens, re-scope to skeptic briefs only (fixed claim inputs, enum verdict) at a pinned commit.

verdicts.reason: I could run the trial on data already in the repo (docs/program/evidence/w2/*.json @3415b5e). likelihood_for_this_fleet has 53 values spread over 17 distinct values, and the top three cover 15/53 (28%), so the '>80% on ≤3 values' condition already fails. FINDINGS.confidence (139 values) sits 81% in 0.7–0.9 and carries little information, but neither number drives any script decision: skeptics are allocated by severity (§4.6.2) and G2 re-sets severity. Replacing a number nothing reads changes nothing.
verdicts.what_would_change_verdict: A script or gate that routes on likelihood or confidence, or a join against skeptic outcomes showing such a routed number predicts nothing.

verdicts.reason: 'Replay the brief and diff the objects' needs live model calls, so it is not the no-model replay of D-10 that the card cites. The inputs (repo and web) have moved since the saved runs, and run-to-run variance (T-03's own lesson) would swamp verdict and severity diffs on open-ended lanes. The source is bullet points with no data.
verdicts.what_would_change_verdict: A brief whose inputs are fixed and pinned (for example a skeptic given a frozen claim) and whose outputs repeat stably at a pinned commit.

verdicts.reason: I confirmed the README quotes. 'An unknown is not zero' is RT-06 (HARNESS-REVIEW:281). 'A check must be able to fail' is RT-01 and the KS inject-control rule, under which controls must flip. Repeats only matter inside B-13, which is refuted.

verdicts.reason: The tier split is an owner standing rule. The evidence is an auto-generated transcript read through an extractor, with demo thresholds. The check means paying Opus to redo a Sonnet lane, and diffs of open-ended cards do not converge on anything. No routing failure has been recorded.
verdicts.what_would_change_verdict: A recorded case where a Sonnet lane missed something an Opus pass later found, and it changed a decision.

verdicts.reason: Transcripts are reachable (agent-<id>.jsonl), but the recorded quota failures came from fan-out size and effort, and the recorded remedy is 'Keep the fan-out small and the effort default' (HANDOFF §5.5), not cutting waste inside agents. Fixed overhead dominates anyway: each subagent starts above 63k prompt tokens (KS design:794). The HR transcript audit found nothing that caused a mistake (HARNESS-REVIEW §6). The yes-threshold counts brief edits, not quality.
verdicts.what_would_change_verdict: A token breakdown showing that wasted tool calls inside agents, not fixed prompt overhead or fan-out, dominate a lane's spend.

verdicts.reason: The 15%-cheaper yes-threshold cannot be reached: the CONTEXT block is a few hundred tokens against a starting prompt above 63k tokens per subagent (KS design:794). The cited win came from a runtime tool (baml describe) we do not have, and the episode gives no counts.
verdicts.what_would_change_verdict: A measurement showing the CONTEXT block, or the brief prose, is a material share of a subagent's input tokens.

verdicts.reason: Free and transferable, but the benefit is unrecorded and the proposed hard checks misfire on real data. A naive 'path:line — quote' regex flags 174 of 707 evidence strings in the accepted W2 outputs (docs/program/evidence/w2/*.json @3415b5e), mostly legitimate library-path, command and web forms. The quotes I checked against their sources in this run were all present and within 15 words. Checking that a quote is really in its source is already done by the §4.6.1 citation check and the §4.6.3 web re-check. The bounded retry adds pressure to fabricate: a fresh agent that never fetched the page can shorten a quote just to pass.
verdicts.what_would_change_verdict: Run record-only checks (no retry) over the committed raw outputs. Adopt if they find real violations the gates missed. Format rules that a schema pattern or maxLength can express belong in the schema instead.

verdicts.reason: §5.2 already has escape hatches: UNVERIFIABLE, untestable, UNCLEAR, in_field_apk 'unknown', corrected_severity NONE, exit_code -1 for 'not run', and '' where allowed. An empty RESEARCH result is valid, and RT-06 says unknown is recorded as unknown, never 0. This run's readers wrote 'undated' honestly. The source is an interview whose host discloses an investment in Boundary.

verdicts.reason: It conflicts with ORCHESTRATION-DESIGN:326: REFUTED requires positive counter-evidence that the skeptic finds itself, and restricting citations to handed-in ids would forbid exactly that. Fabricated citations are already caught by the §4.6.1 citation check and the §4.6.3 web re-check. No fabricated URL has been recorded in a verification step, and the source has no measurement.

verdicts.reason: The docs caveat is confirmed, but nothing is left to do. Tool-layer validation would reject case drift (the card concedes this). No §5 enum differs only by case (P0–P3, CONFIRMED…, supported…, FIXED…, LOCATED…). verdicts.reason: This is Pydantic AI prior art, not BAML. Refute if Workflow scripts cannot route calls through a stub.

prior_claim_challenge: 'ideas_not_tool' stands as far as it goes, but it gives BAML too much credit, and its proof is mis-specified. (1) After refutation, the ideas left standing (I-13, D-13, T-08, P-10) come from Anthropic's docs, standard JSON Schema and Pydantic AI prior art, not from BAML. Most BAML-sourced cards restate what §4.3, §5 and RT-06 already do. The honest answer is neither the tool nor distinctive ideas. (2) The harness proof is pinned to B-13, which is refuted here, so it compares against a trial that should not run. The real precondition is missing: whether BAML can run under the owner's Claude Code auth at all. BAML clients call provider APIs with keys, which would be a second billing and egress path (inferred, not verified this run). (3) The product proof measures accuracy on the values returned, which is the metric SAP's silent array drop flatters (issue #4590, confirmed). It must also count dropped rows against an expected count. Area (d) stays moot because no LLM feature is planned.
